issue_context.title: powerReports not handling null value in smartthings
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Missed a `None` guard for powerReports that have a null value.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.8.0b8

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

smartthings

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/smartthings/

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
2021-08-02 12:20:15 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.sensor] Error adding entities for domain sensor with platform smartthings
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 382, in async_add_entities
    await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 587, in _async_add_entity
    await entity.add_to_platform_finish()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 711, in add_to_platform_finish
    self.async_write_ha_state()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 464, in async_write_ha_state
    self._async_write_ha_state()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 498, in _async_write_ha_state
    state = self._stringify_state()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 470, in _stringify_state
    state = self.state
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/smartthings/sensor.py", line 572, in state
    if value.get(self.report_name) is None:
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'
```


### Additional information

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/53888 created to fix it.

review_comments:
We should only return this when report name is energy, not power.

Also please include the comment in the code that it's an exception.

as already discussed here https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/53759#discussion_r680026699 and https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/53759#discussion_r680630611 the `SmartThingsPowerConsumptionSensor` should not set `STATE_CLASS_MEASUREMENT`
we're making an exception because it's close enough.
I am aware, balloob stated this is an exception.
